newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak government approves new banking law.
newsitem.headline: Slovak government approves new banking law.

text.p: The Slovak government on Tuesday approved a new banking law which scraps the former three percent limit on foreigners holding stakes in domestic banks, Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said.

The new law, which still must be approved by the parliament, will retain the obligation to request the central bank's (NBS) approval for increasing holdings of one entity in a bank at over 10, 20, 33, and 50 percent.
"The law will equalise positions of domestic and foreign entities within the rules for holdings of banks' basic capital," Kozlik told a news conference.
Kozlik said the law could become effective in October or November this year, adding the date will depend on final approval by the parliament.
The new law will also change procedures for requesting the banking licence.
Under current legislation, state authorities must first approve a request for the creation of a bank, and then they also have to grant a licence for carrying out banking operations.
The new law combines the two procedures into one move.

"The new banking law will get our legislation closer to OECD standards and help us with integration into this organisation," Kozlik said. Slovakia hopes to win OECD membership by the end of this year.
